thread:
sam: FYI I flipped a canary to marlin-ptq-v2 (int6) for a small subset of onboard traffic. Quick sanity sweep shows 97.8% structured-output pass but a weird class of partial-jsons at tail.

jules: Saw the same. Repro snippet from logs (truncated):
```
{"action":"create_ticket","params":{"title":"Order failed","user_id":12345}
...<stream cut>
```
parser error: unexpected EOF when expecting '}'

maya: ugh, trailing cutoffs. Are these all streaming responses or both streaming + non-streaming? Any correlation with batch size?

sam: Mostly streaming (continuous-mode). Non-streaming looks fine in the small sample. Batch size for canary is 4, max_seq 1024.

kai: Looks like KV-cache alignment shift on the int6 kernel path — we saw token dropping on previous PTQ builds when sequence boundaries hit certain attention kernel thresholds.

nora: Could be a streaming flush race. If the last chunk is dropped during a worker preemption we get truncated JSON. Do we have worker preempt counts during the window?

jules: Attached quick metric: preempt spikes + network backpressure coincide. Also saw a few entries with double-eos markers: "\u0003\u0003" which our streamer sometimes treats as EOF twice.

maya: Two angles: 1) short-term rescue for downstream parsers: append heuristic close brace and attempt JSON repair. 2) long-term: make streamer ensure final chunk with explicit sentinel/\n\n.

sam: For short-term we can enable json-healer in the client for the canary only. But want to avoid masking regressions for full rollout.

kai: Recommend toggling canary to non-streaming for a minute to confirm if it's streaming-only. If non-streaming passes, that's strong signal.

jules: I just flipped the canary to sync-mode for 10% of traffic (kept rest streaming). Will monitor parse_fail_rate.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy marlin-ptq-v2 -> 2026-03-23T15:34:10Z (id: cd3f2a)

nora: Also propose we add a retry-budget exception: if parse fails and response length > 128 tokens, let caller retry once with sync mode. Won't count against user quota for canary.

maya: +1. Also let's capture the last 8 tokens of the model output in a masked log (no PII) for debug — helps verify whether kernel trimmed tokens or streamer dropped them.

sam: OK plan: 1) enable sync-mode probe 10% (jules done), 2) enable client json-healer for canary, 3) add one-time retry budget for parse fails, 4) collect end-of-stream token snippets. I'll run an eval harness comparing structured-output pass rate across int8/int6/float baseline after 2h.

jules: I'll wire the metrics: parse_fail_rate, preempt_count, last_chunk_length, double_eos_count. Expect to have a dashboard within 30m.

kai: If this confirms kernel misalignment, next step is a microquant rebuild with alignment fix and a tiny PTQ re-run.

nora: Good. If anyone sees a clear non-streaming failure ping me and I can grab core dumps from the worker.

maya: thanks — will post the eval diffs once the harness finishes. :eyes:

sam: Nice work team. Keeping this canary tight. Also tagging infra to watch for correlated VM evictions. @infra? (not in thread)
